chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the slave who is emancipated unconditionally (sa'ibah).

He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is under the guardianship of whomever he desires, and upon the one who is guardian is his liability (for debts/crimes), and for him is his inheritance.' We said to him (peace be upon him): 'So if he remains silent until he dies and does not appoint anyone as guardian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.جَرِيرَة: Liability / debt / responsibility (often for debts or minor crimes).
key_terms.سَائِبَة: An unconditionally freed slave who is not bound to a specific master or condition.
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّى: To be under the guardianship of / to appoint a guardian.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an unconditionally freed slave (sa'ibah) who dies without appointing a guardian?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal mechanism for a 'sa'ibah' (unconditionally freed slave) to select a patron (mawla) who assumes both guardianship and inheritance rights, reflecting the Shia emphasis on voluntary social bonds. The Imam clarifies that if no patron is chosen before death, the estate reverts to the public treasury (bayt al-mal), ensuring social welfare and preventing asset forfeiture. This ruling underscores the importance of lineage and social integration in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Shuayb Al Aqarqufy, from Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the slave emancipating a slave unconditionally.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be his guardian whoever he so desires, and upon the one who is guardian are his crimes, and for him would be his inheritance’. We said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if remains such until he dies and no one is his guardian?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His wealth would be made to be in the public treasury of the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Shu’ayb al-‘Aqarqufiy from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the slave who is freed as Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave).

He (the Imam) said, ‘He is free to find a guardian of his choosing and on whoever he chooses as his guardian are his liabilities for his crimes and for him is his legacy.’ We then asked, ‘What happens if he remains quiet until he dies and does not take anyone as his guardian?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘His legacy is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.’”
